rows.technology: FoundationModels — guided generation (@Generable) + tool calling, macOS 26 baseline
rows.claim: FoundationModels on macOS 26 provides @Generable constrained decoding into Swift types with 'strong guarantees that the response is in a format you expect' and a Tool protocol, with a documented 4,096-token context window and 26.4-added SystemLanguageModel.contextSize and tokenCount(for:) pre-measurement APIs.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/languagemodelsession/generationerror/exceededcontextwindowsize(_:) — 'LanguageModelSession.GenerationError.exceededContextWindowSize(_:)' (states the 4,096-token context window); corroborated by https://developer.apple.com/documentation/updates/foundationmodels — 'Foundation Models updates' (Feb 2026 entry: contextSize + tokenCount in 26.4) and https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/generable — 'Generable'
rows.availability: macOS 26.0+ (contextSize/tokenCount need 26.4); Apple Silicon Mac with Apple Intelligence enabled; Apple Intelligence region/language gating applies — check SystemLanguageModel.availability at runtime; no special entitlement for the base model
rows.distribution_impact: None beyond building against the macOS 26 SDK; works from a bare CLI binary (no app bundle or entitlement), compatible with the Homebrew build-from-source story
rows.permissions: No TCC prompt; requires the user to have Apple Intelligence turned on (detectable via the availability API, not a permission dialog)
rows.fail_closed: Yes — SystemLanguageModel.availability plus typed GenerationErrors (context overflow, guardrails) mean unavailability degrades to no-suggestion; guided generation's enum constraint prevents the model from inventing a destination folder
rows.privacy: Fully on-device inference; prompts and file names never leave the Mac
rows.testability: 10-line Swift script on this Mac (macOS 26.6): check SystemLanguageModel.default.availability, run one respond() call with a @Generable enum of the 5 DeskTidy folders, print model.contextSize and tokenCount(for:) on the same prompt
rows.corrections: The cited exceededContextWindowSize symbol is deprecated as of the macOS 27 beta docset in favor of LanguageModelError.contextSizeExceeded(_:) — write new code against the newer error surface. The rate-limiting claim is confirmed only by an Apple Frameworks Engineer forum reply (thread 789788: limits apply on battery + background; known issue on power), which is not documentation — BELIEVED. The '~3B' parameter figure comes from the WWDC25 video (3B, 2-bit quantized), not API docs — BELIEVED. The updates page also warns the underlying model changes at 26.4 and 27.0, so prompts must be retested per OS model version — the roadmap did not mention this.

rows.technology: FoundationModels — custom LoRA adapters (adapter training toolkit)
rows.claim: Apple's adapter training toolkit trains LoRA adapters for the on-device model (Apple Silicon Mac ≥32GB or Linux GPU, Python 3.11+), each adapter is ~160MB, pinned to a single system model version, must be server-hosted and delivered via Background Assets rather than bundled, requires the Foundation Models Framework Adapter Entitlement, and loads via SystemLanguageModel(adapter:guardrails:).
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/apple-intelligence/foundation-models-adapter/ — 'Adapter training toolkit for Apple Foundation Models' (confirms LoRA method, 32GB Mac/Linux GPU, ~160MB per adapter, per-model-version retraining, host-don't-bundle via Background Assets, entitlement requirement)
rows.availability: Runtime API present in the macOS 26 SDK (observed in the macOS 26.6 SDK swiftinterface on this Mac); training needs an Apple Silicon Mac with ≥32GB or a Linux GPU box; deployment needs an Apple Developer Program entitlement grant; each adapter binds to one exact system model version
rows.distribution_impact: Heavy — adapters cannot ship in the app bundle; requires a hosting server, a Background Assets download pipeline, an entitlement application, and one adapter per supported OS model version; incompatible with DeskTidy's Homebrew source-build, zero-network distribution
rows.permissions: Foundation Models Framework Adapter Entitlement (must be requested from Apple); network access for adapter download
rows.fail_closed: Yes at the API level — SystemLanguageModel.Adapter.AssetError includes compatibleAdapterNotFound/invalidAsset (observed in SDK), so a stale adapter fails explicitly rather than silently degrading
rows.privacy: Inference is on-device, but the mandatory hosted-download delivery introduces a network surface contrary to DeskTidy's local-only, zero-network posture
rows.testability: Not worth a spike given REJECT; if ever revisited: compile a 5-line reference to SystemLanguageModel.Adapter against the macOS 26 SDK (symbol presence already observed in /Applications/Xcode.app/...MacOSX.sdk FoundationModels swiftinterface, lines 585/652)
rows.corrections: Both original citations were secondary: the GitHub mirror is a snapshot of an Apple article ('Loading and using a custom adapter with Foundation Models') that now 301-redirects to the FoundationModels framework root, and Adapter symbols are absent from the current online docset (macOS 27-beta reorg) even though the API exists in the macOS 26.6 SDK — the lane is less stable than the roadmap implied; the provide.ai citation is dead (HTTP 404). The roadmap also omitted the required adapter entitlement, which strengthens the skip. Primary source located (toolkit page, live on developer.apple.com).

rows.technology: FoundationModels — WWDC26 multimodal image input, Spotlight RAG, provider abstraction (macOS 27 beta)
rows.claim: The macOS 27 beta FoundationModels adds image prompting (NSImage/CGImage/pixel buffer/URL) with Vision-backed OCRTool and BarcodeReaderTool, a Spotlight-powered local RAG search tool, a LanguageModel provider protocol that can route sessions to third-party models (Anthropic/Google) or PrivateCloudCompute (32K context), and an official Python SDK.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/languagemodel — 'LanguageModel' (macOS 27.0, beta) + https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/analyzing-images-with-multimodal-prompting — 'Analyzing images with multimodal prompting' + https://developer.apple.com/documentation/updates/foundationmodels — 'Foundation Models updates' (June 2026 section, links apple/python-apple-fm-sdk)
rows.availability: macOS 27 beta only today (GA expected ~fall 2026 — expectation, not documented); on-device multimodal hardware floor not stated in any primary source; PCC and third-party provider lanes require network and accounts
rows.distribution_impact: Requires building against the macOS 27 SDK and excludes every macOS 26 customer today — adopting now would break DeskTidy's honest-claims rule
rows.permissions: On-device lanes: none; PCC/third-party provider lanes: network plus provider credentials
rows.fail_closed: Same availability-check pattern as macOS 26 for the on-device lane; the provider-abstraction and PCC lanes are inherently network-dependent and cannot fail closed into a local-only guarantee
