rows.testability: On a macOS 27 beta VM or spare partition: 5-line spike from the 'Analyzing images with multimodal prompting' article prompting the on-device model with one screenshot URL; separately confirm the OS-26 code path still compiles untouched
rows.corrections: The '~20B sparse model that ships on high-end hardware only' sub-claim appears in NO primary Apple source (the WWDC26 session 241 page and the beta docs are silent on parameter count and hardware floor) and the byteiota citation is currently unreachable (connection failure) — that sub-claim is UNKNOWN. Apple's materials name Anthropic/Google as provider examples rather than literally 'Gemini or Claude'. Verified additions the roadmap missed: PCC server model documented at 32K-token context; WWDC26 videos are Apple-authored but not API contracts — the beta doc pages above are the real contract, and they are marked beta, so nothing here is adoptable for macOS 26 buyers.

rows.technology: Vision framework — OCR: RecognizeTextRequest + RecognizeDocumentsRequest (macOS 26)
rows.claim: RecognizeTextRequest (macOS 15+) and RecognizeDocumentsRequest (macOS 26.0, released) do fully on-device OCR with structured output — words/lines/paragraphs, tables, lists, and barcodes per the API docs, plus typed detected data (emails/phone numbers/URLs) — with 30 recognition languages measured on this Mac.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/recognizedocumentsrequest — 'RecognizeDocumentsRequest' (macOS 26.0, released; confirms structure groups, tables, lists, barcodes) + https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/recognizetextrequest — 'RecognizeTextRequest' (macOS 15.0)
rows.availability: macOS 26.0 for RecognizeDocumentsRequest, macOS 15.0 for RecognizeTextRequest; any Apple Silicon Mac; no Apple Intelligence dependency (Vision framework, not FoundationModels)
rows.distribution_impact: None — links against the system Vision framework and runs headless from a CLI binary (verified: swift script executed the API on this Mac without an app bundle); Homebrew story intact
rows.permissions: None beyond the file-read access the process already has; respects existing TCC scoping
rows.fail_closed: Yes — throwing async API; OCR failure yields no suggestion, and all downstream behavior is deterministic user-visible rules with logging, never automatic mutation
rows.privacy: Fully local; screenshot contents never leave the Mac
rows.testability: swift script on this Mac: run RecognizeDocumentsRequest on one real ~/Desktop screenshot, print transcript + detectedData matches; language-enumeration spike already run (supportedRecognitionLanguages = 30 on macOS 26.6)
rows.corrections: The '26 languages' figure was the WWDC25 session number; I measured 30 supported recognition languages on macOS 26.6 — the roadmap undersold it. The detected-data detail (emails/phones/URLs) was confirmed in WWDC25 session 272 (video, not an API contract) but the DocumentObservation API surface backing it is in the released docs. The createwithswift citation is secondary and consistent; primary docs now anchor the row.

rows.technology: Vision framework — ClassifyImageRequest (image/scene classification)
rows.claim: ClassifyImageRequest (macOS 15.0, released) is an on-device multi-label classifier returning ClassificationObservation identifier+confidence pairs, with 1303 supported class identifiers measured on macOS 26.6 — including exactly the labels DeskTidy's example rules need: 'document', 'receipt', 'whiteboard', 'screenshot'.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vision/classifyimagerequest — 'ClassifyImageRequest' (macOS 15.0, released)
rows.availability: macOS 15.0+; any Apple Silicon Mac; no Apple Intelligence dependency; runs headless from a CLI process (observed)
rows.distribution_impact: None — system framework, works in the bare Homebrew CLI today and in the future menu-bar app
rows.permissions: None beyond existing file-read access
rows.fail_closed: Yes — throwing API; classifier output is data feeding user-authored deterministic threshold rules, logged with label+confidence, suggestions-only in the CLI
rows.privacy: Fully local
rows.testability: Vocabulary spike already run on this Mac (supportedIdentifiers = 1303, containing document/receipt/whiteboard/screenshot); next smallest spike: classify 5 real desktop screenshots and print top-3 labels+confidence to see whether ≥0.8 thresholds are realistic
rows.corrections: Both original citations (createwithswift, zhgchg.li) are secondary and neither states the class count — the '~1000 classes' figure was uncited; measured 1303 on this Mac, so the claim was roughly right but unanchored. Primary Apple doc located and now anchors the row. The doc does not publish the label taxonomy — supportedIdentifiers must be queried at runtime, which also means the vocabulary can shift across OS releases (log the OS version with each classification).

rows.technology: Core Spotlight — CSSearchableItem donation + CSUserQuery semantic search
rows.claim: An app can donate CSSearchableItems (macOS 10.11+) and query them with CSUserQuery, which the current doc describes as performing 'lexical and semantic searches' with ranked results (CSUserQuery macOS 13+; the semantic pieces — prepare(), disableSemanticSearch — macOS 15+), while developer forums report the semantic layer failing with embedding-generation timeouts for over a year.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corespotlight/csuserquery — 'CSUserQuery' (overview states lexical and semantic search) + https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corespotlight/csuserquery/prepare() (macOS 15.0) + https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corespotlight/cssearchableitem (macOS 10.11)
rows.availability: Donation macOS 10.11+, CSUserQuery macOS 13+, semantic additions macOS 15+; requires a real app bundle with a bundle identifier — not reachable from the bare Homebrew CLI, so it lands with the menu-bar app as the roadmap says
rows.distribution_impact: Needs the signed/notarized menu-bar .app; no server or entitlement; the CLI cannot ship this
rows.permissions: None special; the app writes only to its own Spotlight index
rows.fail_closed: Yes — donation is purely additive metadata about already-completed logged moves; index or query failure degrades to no search results and never touches file operations
rows.privacy: On-device Spotlight index; donated move-log metadata (filenames, destinations, rules, timestamps) stays local
rows.testability: Scratch app bundle on this Mac: donate 3 CSSearchableItems representing fake move-log entries, run a lexical CSUserQuery, then call CSUserQuery.prepare() and re-run with semantic enabled to diff results — directly probes the forum-reported breakage before any marketing claim
rows.corrections: The core donation+query plan is fully documented and stable; the reality-check sub-claim (semantic layer non-functional) rests on forum thread 793867 — verified to report exactly that (EmbeddingModelError -8007 100ms timeouts, reversed disableSemanticSearch logic where true enables it, sample app never released, no Apple response) — but forums are secondary, so that part is BELIEVED pending the live probe. WWDC24 session 10131 (video) is corroboration, not the contract; the CSUserQuery API doc is the primary anchor and does state semantic search. Ship lexical-only claims until the probe passes, as the roadmap already intended.

rows.technology: NaturalLanguage — NLEmbedding / NLContextualEmbedding
rows.claim: NLEmbedding (macOS 10.15+, sentence embeddings macOS 11+) maps strings to vectors with neighbor lookup and documented cosine distance, and NLContextualEmbedding (macOS 14+) computes contextual token-embedding sequences on-device after a one-time per-language asset download.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/naturallanguage/nlcontextualembedding — "NLContextualEmbedding"; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/naturallanguage/nlembedding — "NLEmbedding"; cosine: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/naturallanguage/nldistancetype/cosine
rows.availability: NLEmbedding: macOS 10.15+; sentenceEmbedding(for:): macOS 11+; NLContextualEmbedding: macOS 14+ with downloadable per-language model assets (hasAvailableAssets / requestAssets documented). No Apple Intelligence or special-hardware requirement documented.
rows.distribution_impact: None — ships in the OS, no entitlement; callable from the existing brew-distributed CLI as well as a future menu-bar app.
rows.permissions: None documented; no TCC prompt.
rows.fail_closed: Check hasAvailableAssets before embedding; if assets are missing or the language is unsupported the engine emits no suggestion and DeskTidy falls back to deterministic rules — suggests-only preserved.
rows.privacy: Embeddings computed entirely on-device; filenames never leave the Mac. Asset download contacts Apple servers to fetch the model, not user data.
rows.testability: 15-line Swift script: NLEmbedding.wordEmbedding(for: .english) → print dimension and neighbors(for: "invoice", maximumCount: 5); then NLContextualEmbedding(language: .english), hasAvailableAssets, embeddingResult(for:) on a filename token; run twice and diff vectors to confirm determinism.
rows.corrections: "Static 512-dim vectors" is not in Apple's docs — dimensionality is exposed only via the queryable `dimension` property (the 512 figure traces to WWDC-era/secondary sources like the cited Callstack blog). Mean-pooling contextual token vectors into sentence vectors is a developer technique, not a documented API feature. Contextual embeddings are not download-free: a one-time per-language asset fetch is required.

rows.technology: Image Playground / Genmoji (ImagePlayground framework, ImageCreator API)
rows.claim: ImageCreator (macOS 15.4+; framework sheet APIs macOS 15.1+) generates images programmatically from descriptions and styles, and throws Error.notSupported on devices lacking the hardware required to run the generation models.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/imageplayground/imagecreator — "ImageCreator"; framework: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/imageplayground — "Image Playground"
rows.availability: Framework macOS 15.1+; ImageCreator macOS 15.4+. Gated on image-generation-capable hardware (ImageCreator.Error.notSupported: "Make sure the device has the hardware required to run models"); in practice tied to Apple Intelligence enablement (Apple Silicon, supported region/language) per Apple support pages, not the API reference.
rows.distribution_impact: Would shrink the addressable base to Apple Intelligence-capable, enabled Macs and add a generative-image dependency to a file-organizer — moot since deferred.
rows.permissions: User must have Apple Intelligence enabled; no TCC prompt documented for the API itself.
rows.fail_closed: API fails closed by design: Error.notSupported / Error.unavailable thrown when generation cannot run — feature is simply absent, nothing degrades silently.
rows.privacy: Generation runs via Apple's on-device model stack; no DeskTidy user data involved since the roadmap ships nothing on this.
rows.testability: 10-line Swift spike on this Mac: try await ImageCreator() and catch notSupported/unavailable, then one prompt→image round-trip if enabled — confirms the availability gate in under a minute.
rows.corrections: Original cited only a secondary blog (createwithswift) plus a WWDC26 video (session 375 exists — "Create high-quality images using Image Playground" — but is not an API contract). Primary API doc exists and confirms macOS 15.4+ for ImageCreator. "Apple Intelligence required" is Apple marketing/support-page framing; the API reference itself gates on device hardware via Error.notSupported. Verdict mapped skip→DEFER (no DeskTidy invariant is violated; it is simply useless here and muddies the local-only, suggests-only story).

rows.technology: Speech (SpeechAnalyzer / SpeechTranscriber, macOS 26) + SoundAnalysis
rows.claim: SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber (macOS 26.0+ only) perform speech-to-text on files and audio streams using downloadable per-locale assets, and SoundAnalysis's SNClassifySoundRequest (macOS 10.15+; built-in classifier version1 macOS 12+) classifies sounds via a Core ML model.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechanalyzer — "SpeechAnalyzer"; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechtranscriber — "SpeechTranscriber"; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/soundanalysis/snclassifysoundrequest — "SNClassifySoundRequest"
rows.availability: SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber: macOS 26.0+ only, per-locale assets downloadable (supportedLocales vs installed distinction documented). SoundAnalysis: macOS 10.15+, built-in classifier version1 macOS 12+. No Apple Intelligence requirement documented.
rows.distribution_impact: Would raise the minimum OS to macOS 26 for the transcription feature; per-file transcription is the highest per-item compute cost of any option surveyed — moot since deferred.
rows.permissions: File-based transcription shows no documented TCC prompt; microphone capture (not DeskTidy's use case) would require mic permission.
rows.fail_closed: Unsupported locale/OS or missing assets → no transcription result; deterministic extension routing of audio files to Audio/ continues unchanged.
rows.privacy: Transcription and classification run on-device; audio never uploaded. Locale asset download contacts Apple servers.
rows.testability: On a macOS 26 machine: Swift spike transcribing a 10-second WAV via SpeechAnalyzer+SpeechTranscriber (measure wall time), then SNClassifySoundRequest(classifierIdentifier: .version1) on the same file to enumerate returned classes.
rows.corrections: Both original citations were secondary (Callstack blog, GitHub example). "~2x Whisper Large V3 Turbo" is a third-party benchmark, not Apple-documented — BELIEVED at best. "~300 sound classes" does not appear in the current SNClassifySoundRequest/version1 reference; it traces to a WWDC21 session — BELIEVED. Core availability and API surface confirmed against primary docs; verdict mapped skip→DEFER (poor ROI now, no invariant violated; the voice-memo-naming nugget remains a legitimate future opt-in).

rows.technology: QuickLookThumbnailing — QLThumbnailGenerator
rows.claim: QLThumbnailGenerator (macOS 10.15+) generates thumbnails for arbitrary file URLs via generateBestRepresentation(for:) and progressive generateRepresentations(for:update:), using the system Quick Look machinery, read-only and with no ML.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quicklookthumbnailing/qlthumbnailgenerator — "QLThumbnailGenerator"
rows.availability: macOS 10.15+; no special hardware, region, or entitlement requirements documented.
rows.distribution_impact: None — works from both the current CLI and a future menu-bar app; no entitlement or bundle requirement.
rows.permissions: None beyond ordinary file read access to the target URL.
rows.fail_closed: On generation failure the request errors or returns only the icon representation; UI shows a generic icon. Read-only — no file mutation possible, so no invariant is even reachable.
rows.privacy: Thumbnails generated locally by system Quick Look plugins; no network involved.
rows.testability: 10-line Swift spike: QLThumbnailGenerator.shared.generateRepresentations(for: Request(fileAt: <a Desktop PNG>, size: 64x64, scale: 2, representationTypes: .all)) and log the callback order (icon → thumbnail) to confirm progressive delivery.
rows.corrections: Both original citations were secondary (Medium post, Apple forums thread). Primary doc confirms macOS 10.15+ and both generate methods. The truncated watch-item is real: forum thread 805177 reports QLThumbnailGenerator serving stale cached folder icons on macOS 26 with no public cache-invalidation API, community-confirmed fixed in macOS 26.4 (BELIEVED — forum-sourced, not in Apple release notes). Verdict mapped adopt-in-menubar-app→ADOPT: core claim is DOCUMENTED and needs no live probe before commitment.

rows.technology: SMAppService (ServiceManagement framework)
rows.claim: SMAppService (macOS 13+) registers login items, launch agents (agent(plistName:) with the plist embedded at Contents/Library/LaunchAgents inside the app bundle), and daemons via register()/unregister()/status, with services user-visible and toggleable in System Settings' Login Items panel (openSystemSettingsLoginItems documented).
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/servicemanagement/smappservice — "SMAppService"; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/servicemanagement/smappservice/agent(plistname:) — "agent(plistName:)"
rows.availability: macOS 13.0+; no hardware or region constraints; requires shipping a real .app bundle to host the embedded agent plist.
rows.distribution_impact: Replaces DeskTidy's two hand-installed ~/Library/LaunchAgents plists but requires moving distribution from bare brew CLI to an .app bundle (or brew cask); uninstall must call unregister() instead of deleting plists.
rows.permissions: User approval surface built in: status can report .requiresApproval, and the user can disable the agent any time in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions.
rows.fail_closed: status API lets the app detect not-registered/not-approved and report honestly; if the user toggles the agent off, the watcher simply never launches — no watcher means no moves, which is DeskTidy's fail-closed state.
rows.privacy: No user data involved; registration is user-visible in System Settings — a transparency improvement over mystery plists.
rows.testability: Minimal .app with one embedded agent plist (BundleProgram → echo script): call SMAppService.agent(plistName:).register(), assert status == .enabled, confirm the entry appears in System Settings Login Items, then unregister() and confirm removal.
rows.corrections: None — the original row was already primary-sourced and accurate; re-verified today: macOS 13+ availability, Contents/Library/LaunchAgents embedding (stated on the agent(plistName:) page), and System Settings Login Items visibility all confirmed in current Apple docs. The secondary theevilbit post was corroborating, not load-bearing.

rows.technology: UNUserNotificationCenter (UserNotifications framework)
rows.claim: UNUserNotificationCenter (macOS 10.14+) is Apple's current notification API — NSUserNotification is documented as deprecated since macOS 11.0 — scoped to "your app or app extension", with authorization prompts and custom action buttons (UNNotificationAction) wired to app code.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unusernotificationcenter — "UNUserNotificationCenter"; deprecation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsusernotification (introduced 10.8, deprecated 11.0)
rows.availability: macOS 10.14+; requires a real app bundle with a bundle ID — not usable from a bare CLI binary.
rows.distribution_impact: Same .app-bundle shift as F11: the menu-bar app posts notifications as DeskTidy with Undo/Open-in-Finder actions; terminal-notifier/osascript remain the only options for the bare-CLI install path.
rows.permissions: Explicit user authorization prompt (requestAuthorization); per-app entry in System Settings > Notifications where the user can silence or disable.
rows.fail_closed: Authorization denied or notification undelivered → moves are still logged and undoable from the app UI; notifications are a courtesy layer, never the mutation path or the record of it.
rows.privacy: Notification content (filenames, destinations) stays local; note filenames may appear on the lock screen subject to the user's notification-preview settings.
rows.testability: Two-part spike: (1) minimal .app bundle — requestAuthorization, post "Moved x to y" with an Undo UNNotificationAction, verify the handler fires; (2) run the identical code as a bare binary and confirm the bundleProxyForCurrentProcess crash, proving the bundle requirement.
rows.corrections: The API surface, macOS 10.14+ availability, and NSUserNotification's macOS 11.0 deprecation are all confirmed in primary Apple docs. The specific 'bundleProxyForCurrentProcess is nil' CLI crash is confirmed real in forum thread 724249 but is community-sourced with no official doc stating the bundle requirement explicitly (the reference's "app or app extension" scoping implies it) — that detail is BELIEVED. terminal-notifier's packaged-as-.app rationale rests on its GitHub repo (secondary).

rows.technology: App Intents + Shortcuts + Siri + Spotlight actions (macOS 26)
rows.claim: On macOS Tahoe 26, App Intents actions run directly from Spotlight and Mac Shortcuts gained automations (time-of-day, save-file-to-folder, display-connect), so exposing DeskTidy's verbs as intents is annotation work over documented, public APIs.
rows.primary_source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/macos-tahoe-26-makes-the-mac-more-capable-productive-and-intelligent-than-ever/ — 'macOS Tahoe 26 makes the Mac more capable, productive, and intelligent than ever' (Apple Newsroom). Corroborating WWDC26 video (macOS 27 cycle): https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/240/ — 'Build intelligent Siri experiences with App Schemas'.
rows.availability: macOS 26 (Tahoe) for Spotlight-invoked App Intents and Mac Shortcuts automations; runs on any Tahoe-capable Mac (Apple Silicon or supported Intel); requires a real .app bundle. No special entitlement to define/run intents. The Siri/Apple-Intelligence-takes-in-app-actions layer (App Schemas) targets the '27 releases,' i.e. macOS 27, not Tahoe 26.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires shipping a real .app bundle; the bare Homebrew CLI cannot vend App Intents. No Mac App Store requirement — works under Developer ID. This is the finding's main gating cost: it lands with the menu-bar app, not the CLI.
rows.permissions: None special to define or run intents; invocation is an explicit user action. No focus/automation entitlement needed for the Spotlight-actions path.
rows.fail_closed: Intents call the same deterministic routing core the UI uses; if Siri/Apple Intelligence is unavailable or disabled, manual/Spotlight invocation still works and nothing auto-mutates. Suggest-only invariant is preserved because an intent is an explicit user command, not a probabilistic trigger.
rows.privacy: Local-only; App Intents and Spotlight-action execution run on-device with no network egress for DeskTidy's use.
rows.testability: Add a single SortNowIntent (AppIntent) to a minimal .app, build against the Xcode 26 SDK, and confirm it appears in Spotlight's Actions browser and runs the core sweep; ~1 day spike.
rows.corrections: The roadmap files a macOS-27 capability under a macOS-26 heading: WWDC26 session 240 ('Build intelligent Siri experiences with App Schemas') frames App Intents as the Siri/Apple-Intelligence action gateway but explicitly targets 'the 27 releases,' not Tahoe 26 — that Siri-action lane is BELIEVED/next-cycle. The Spotlight-run-actions and Shortcuts-automation claims ARE genuinely macOS 26 and Apple-newsroom-documented (verbatim: 'take hundreds of actions directly from Spotlight' and 'run shortcuts automatically... at a specific time of day, or when... saving a file to a folder or connecting a display'). Newsroom says 'any app can provide actions to Spotlight using the App Intents API' but does not itself call App Intents an Apple-Intelligence gateway.

rows.technology: FinderSync extension
rows.claim: FinderSync is a live, not-formally-deprecated but ill-fitting legacy Finder extension point (mutually exclusive with FileProvider) whose System Settings management UI Apple churned during the macOS 15.x cycle, making it a fragile surface for a file utility that is not a sync provider.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/findersync — 'Finder Sync' (Apple Developer Documentation); the 'cannot use both FinderSync and FileProvider extension points; use FileProviderUI for contextual-menu UI' rule is stated on https://developer.apple.com/documentation/findersync/fifindersyncprotocol — 'FIFinderSyncProtocol'.
rows.availability: macOS 10.10+ for FinderSync; ships as an app extension inside a .app. System Settings management UI reportedly removed in macOS 15.0 (Sequoia) and restored in 15.2 (as a 'File Providers' section). No deprecation banner on the Apple doc.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires a .app with an embedded extension; an app cannot ship both FinderSync and FileProvider. Not needed for DeskTidy — Finder presence is better obtained via Quick Actions (F15).
rows.permissions: Extension runs inside Finder's context over watched folder URLs; no special entitlement, but subject to the FinderSync/FileProvider mutual exclusion.
rows.fail_closed: N/A — recommendation is not to adopt; no runtime path introduced.
rows.privacy: Local; would observe watched-folder contents in-process. Not a factor since skipped.
rows.testability: Not worth a spike; a badge-only FinderSync extension in a throwaway .app would confirm the management-UI churn, but the decision is skip regardless.
rows.corrections: The Finder Sync framework is real, public, and NOT formally deprecated (matching the roadmap's 'not formally deprecated' hedge) — that much is Apple-documented. But the load-bearing 'removed in Sequoia, restored in 15.2' churn narrative rests on Michael Tsai's blog (mjtsai.com) and developer-forum posts (secondary), not an Apple release note, so it is BELIEVED, not DOCUMENTED. I could not fetch the live Apple doc body (JS-rendered); the FinderSync/FileProvider mutual-exclusion IS stated in Apple's FIFinderSyncProtocol doc (surfaced via search snippet). Apple's sanctioned replacement for the cloud-sync use case is File Provider, and FileProviderUI covers contextual-menu UI.

rows.technology: Finder Quick Actions / Services menu (Action extension)
rows.claim: An app can bundle an Action extension that appears in Finder's right-click Quick Actions, the Services menu, and (historically) the Touch Bar, operating on selected files — a stable, user-manageable way to route any stray file through DeskTidy's deterministic rules.
rows.primary_source: https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchl97ff9142/mac — 'Perform quick actions in the Finder on Mac' (macOS User Guide, Apple Support). Developer-side Action-extension bundling is documented under Apple's App Extension / Action Extension developer docs (developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/app-extensions).
rows.availability: Quick Actions since macOS Mojave 10.14; still supported on macOS 26. Action extension is bundled inside a .app and is user-manageable in System Settings > Extensions. Requires an app bundle. No special hardware/region gate.
rows.distribution_impact: Small Swift extension target inside the .app; reuses the existing routing engine; no new watcher and no Mac App Store requirement.
rows.permissions: Operates on the files the user explicitly selects and right-clicks — the user's selection is the access grant; no persistent broad-disk permission required for the extension itself.
rows.fail_closed: Every move still goes through the same log/undo path; the action is user-initiated on an explicit selection, so never-delete / everything-logged / suggest-then-act invariants hold.
rows.privacy: Local-only; the extension only sees the user-selected file URLs.
rows.testability: Bundle a trivial Action extension in a test .app that just logs the selected file URLs; confirm it appears under Finder right-click > Quick Actions and in the Services menu, and that it can call the routing core. ~1 day.
rows.corrections: The cited Apple support guide is genuine and confirms the Quick Actions / Services / Touch Bar / Automator-Extensions surfaces (page title 'Perform quick actions in the Finder on Mac'), but it is a user-facing doc — it does not itself document the developer Action-extension bundling; that rests on Apple's App Extension developer docs (still primary Apple, different page). The macosxautomation.com citation is secondary. 'Stable since Mojave, still fully supported' is accurate; note the Touch Bar surface is now largely moot as Touch Bar Macs are discontinued, but that does not affect the Quick Actions/Services value.

rows.technology: Core Spotlight donation (CSSearchableItem / CSSearchableIndex)
rows.claim: Donating each move-log entry via CSSearchableItem/CSSearchableIndex (public since macOS 10.13, with a domain identifier for bulk delete) makes relocated files findable in Spotlight and answers 'where did it go?', but the natural-language LLM-search layer is a macOS 27 (WWDC26) addition, not macOS 26.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corespotlight — 'Core Spotlight' (Apple Developer Documentation). LLM-search lane: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/246/ — 'LLM search using Core Spotlight' (WWDC26 video); WWDC24 semantic layer: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2024/10131/.
rows.availability: Core Spotlight donation (CSSearchableItem/CSSearchableIndex, domainIdentifier): macOS 10.13+. On-device semantic search over donated items: WWDC24 / macOS 15+ (widely reported flaky). LLM search (SpotlightSearchTool + Foundation Models Tool protocol): macOS 27 (WWDC26 cycle), needs Apple-Intelligence-class hardware. All paths require an app bundle.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires a .app bundle to donate content (no extension needed, just the app); no Mac App Store requirement. Lands with the menu-bar app, not the bare CLI.
rows.permissions: None special — the app donates its own content to its own Spotlight index; no user-authorization prompt for donation.
rows.fail_closed: Donation is purely additive read-only metadata; if the index or search fails, files are still moved and logged. No mutation path, so deterministic core is untouched.
rows.privacy: Donated metadata (original name, destination, rule, timestamp) lives in the local on-device Spotlight index; use a 'moves' domainIdentifier and a retention cap so entries can be bulk-deleted/reindexed. No network egress; local-only posture preserved.
rows.testability: Donate one CSSearchableItem with a 'moves' domainIdentifier and a deep link, then confirm it surfaces in Spotlight (lexical) on a macOS 26 Mac; treat the WWDC26 SpotlightSearchTool LLM path as a separate macOS-27 spike.
rows.corrections: Roadmap says 'WWDC26 session 246 LLM search ... makes donated content queryable by on-device LLM search on macOS 26' — this conflates cycles. WWDC26 targets the macOS 27 release; session 246's SpotlightSearchTool rides the WWDC26 Foundation Models updates, so LLM natural-language search over donated content is NOT available on Tahoe 26 (verified: the session and its 'iOS 27 / macOS 27' framing). On macOS 26 you get solid lexical donation plus the WWDC24 semantic layer that other findings and Apple forums report as unreliable. Honest version: adopt the donation + deep-link now (DOCUMENTED, macOS 10.13+); the natural-language 'where did DeskTidy put that invoice' pitch is a macOS-27 (BELIEVED) capability, not a Tahoe feature.

rows.technology: Focus modes / Do Not Disturb (INFocusStatusCenter + SetFocusFilterIntent)
rows.claim: SetFocusFilterIntent (AppIntents, macOS 13+) and INFocusStatusCenter (macOS 12+, com.apple.developer.focus-status entitlement) are the two documented Focus APIs, but a 'pause during Work Focus' filter is low value for DeskTidy since DND already auto-suppresses notifications, and the macOS reliability is questioned.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents/setfocusfilterintent — 'SetFocusFilterIntent' (Apple Developer Documentation); https://developer.apple.com/documentation/intents/infocusstatuscenter — 'INFocusStatusCenter' (Apple Developer Documentation). Reliability report (secondary, Apple-hosted forum): https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/718840.
rows.availability: SetFocusFilterIntent: macOS 13+ via AppIntents (user-configured per Focus). INFocusStatusCenter: macOS 12+, requires the com.apple.developer.focus-status entitlement plus user authorization, and is positioned for communication apps. Requires a .app bundle. DND notification suppression is automatic and needs no code.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires a .app; the focus-status entitlement is aimed at communication apps and may not be readily justifiable/grantable for a file-sorting utility. SetFocusFilterIntent needs no special entitlement but does need the app.
rows.permissions: INFocusStatusCenter: focus-status entitlement + explicit user authorization to read Focus state. SetFocusFilterIntent: no entitlement, user configures the filter in Settings.
rows.fail_closed: DND already suppresses DeskTidy notifications with zero code; a non-firing focus filter degrades to a no-op (sorting simply keeps running / user pauses manually), which is safe and non-destructive.
rows.privacy: Reading Focus status is sensitive user state and is entitlement-gated; skipping avoids collecting it entirely.
rows.testability: Implement a SetFocusFilterIntent that flips a 'paused' flag and, on a macOS 26 Mac, toggle Work Focus to observe whether perform() actually fires — directly reproducing the concern the 2022 forum thread raises before committing.
rows.corrections: The APIs, their macOS availability, and the com.apple.developer.focus-status entitlement are Apple-documented (DOCUMENTED). But the 'perform not called on macOS' rationale driving the skip is a single 2022 Mac Catalyst forum thread with zero replies and no Apple acknowledgment (thread 718840) — a Catalyst-specific, unverified data point, so that reliability claim is BELIEVED, not established as a macOS 26 AppIntents bug. The roadmap's 'flakiest surface on the list' framing overstates a one-post signal. The 'DND auto-suppresses notifications, no code needed' point is correct and is itself a strong reason this feature adds little.

rows.technology: MenuBarExtra (SwiftUI)
rows.claim: MenuBarExtra (macOS 13+) provides the .menu and .window scene styles and, combined with LSUIElement, a no-Dock-icon menu-bar app — a sufficient, documented skeleton for DeskTidy's activity-feed/pause/undo UI, with two known secondary-sourced limitations to design around.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/SwiftUI/MenuBarExtra — 'MenuBarExtra' (Apple Developer Documentation). Limitations (secondary): https://steipete.me/posts/2025/showing-settings-from-macos-menu-bar-items and https://nilcoalescing.com/blog/BuildAMacOSMenuBarUtilityInSwiftUI/.
rows.availability: macOS 13.0+; .menu (default) and .window styles selected via .menuBarExtraStyle(...); pair with the LSUIElement Info.plist key for no Dock icon. Requires a .app bundle. No hardware/region/entitlement gate.
rows.distribution_impact: This is the app skeleton itself — a SwiftUI .app; no Mac App Store requirement. Straightforward Developer ID / notarized distribution.
rows.permissions: None for the menu-bar UI shell.
rows.fail_closed: Pure UI surface; the deterministic sorting core is independent, so UI quirks cannot cause file mutation. Suggest-only and never-delete invariants are unaffected by the shell.
rows.privacy: Local-only UI; no data egress.
rows.testability: Build a MenuBarExtra(.window) app on the Xcode 26 SDK with LSUIElement=YES, confirm the popover renders, and reproduce the SettingsLink/openSettings flakiness firsthand before deciding between the hidden-window workaround and an NSStatusItem wrap. ~1 day.
rows.corrections: MenuBarExtra, its .menu/.window styles (macOS 13+), and LSUIElement are Apple-documented (verified the API and styles via Apple's MenuBarExtra doc). The two cited limitations — SettingsLink/openSettings being unreliable from menu-bar-only apps, and no built-in right-click menu on the status item (needing an NSStatusItem wrap) — rest on Steipete's and Nil Coalescing's blogs (secondary), so those specifics are BELIEVED, not Apple-documented. Steipete does confirm the SettingsLink unreliability firsthand ('doesn't work reliably in MenuBarExtra... documentation doesn't mention this limitation') and prescribes the hidden 1x1 window + activation-policy (.accessory↔.regular) workaround; he does not discuss the right-click/NSStatusItem point, so that part traces to the Nil Coalescing / general community lore.

rows.technology: WidgetKit desktop widgets (macOS)
rows.claim: WidgetKit supports desktop widgets on macOS (Sonoma 14+) and interactive Button/Toggle widgets that run an AppIntent without launching the app, shipped as a widget-extension target inside the app bundle with no App Store requirement.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit/adding-interactivity-to-widgets-and-live-activities — 'Adding interactivity to widgets and Live Activities' (Apple Developer Documentation), which states 'Include buttons or toggles in a widget or Live Activity to offer app functionality without launching the app' and gates Button(intent:) on #available(iOS 17.0,*); overview page https://developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit — 'WidgetKit'.
rows.availability: macOS 14 Sonoma+ (desktop widgets and interactive Button/Toggle widgets share the iOS 17 / macOS 14 baseline); no hardware gate; no entitlement; no MAS/App Store requirement — ships in any Developer ID app.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires an .app bundle with a widget-extension target, so not reachable from the bare Homebrew CLI; lands with the planned menu-bar app as a v1.x addition. Distributable outside the Mac App Store.
rows.permissions: None beyond the host app; the widget's buttons execute in-process App Intents and trigger no additional TCC prompt.
rows.fail_closed: Widget is a read-only status surface plus intent-backed buttons; a failed intent leaves file state unchanged and there is no destructive default action.
rows.privacy: Fully local; the widget renders only app-provided data (recent moves), nothing leaves the device.
rows.testability: Build a minimal WidgetKit extension in a macOS 14+ app exposing a Button(intent: SortNow) plus a recent-moves timeline, place it on the desktop, tap the button, and confirm the intent runs without the app launching.
rows.corrections: No overstatement. 'Interactive since the WWDC23 cycle' is correct (iOS 17 / macOS 14); desktop widgets date from Sonoma (macOS 14). The only load-bearing caveat, already stated in the finding, is that this is app-only (not the CLI) and of modest value.

rows.technology: App Sandbox vs Full Disk Access / TCC UX
rows.claim: The Mac App Store mandates App Sandbox, and a sandboxed always-on background file-mover cannot reach arbitrary user paths (out-of-container access is blocked and Full Disk Access does not bypass the sandbox), so DeskTidy must ship Developer ID + hardened runtime + notarized, outside the MAS — the same lane as Hazel.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/app_sandbox — 'App Sandbox' (Apple Developer Documentation); corroborated by Apple DTS in https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/807142 (DTS Engineer: a sandboxed app 'can only run executables available to its static sandbox' and 'Full Disk Access ... doesn't bypass the App Sandbox checks').
rows.availability: All macOS: App Sandbox is a MAS submission requirement; Developer ID + notarization is available on every macOS with no hardware gate.
rows.distribution_impact: Locks DeskTidy out of the Mac App Store; ship a notarized, hardened-runtime Developer ID DMG (same model as Hazel), which in turn enables the Sparkle updater (F21).
rows.permissions: A non-sandboxed background mover needs Full Disk Access (or the automatic per-folder TCC grants for Desktop/Documents/Downloads) and the FDA drag-in flow for arbitrary rule destinations; no sandbox entitlement is used.
rows.fail_closed: When a required TCC/FDA grant is absent the mover must refuse that path rather than silently fail, routing unknowns to Inbox and logging — consistent with fail-closed.
rows.privacy: Going non-sandboxed with FDA grants broad disk reach; this is the principal privacy-surface tradeoff, mitigated by keeping all activity local and logged and touching only rule-scoped paths.
rows.testability: Build a hardened-runtime, notarized helper WITHOUT the sandbox entitlement, grant it Full Disk Access, and confirm it moves a file from ~/Desktop to ~/Documents; then flip on the App Sandbox entitlement and confirm the same move is blocked by sandboxd.
rows.corrections: The sandbox/MAS/FDA claims are Apple-documented and directly DTS-confirmed. The 'Hazel ships Developer ID, notarized' comparison rests on Noodlesoft's own KB (secondary), not an Apple source — true and widely known but BELIEVED, not primary-sourced; treat the Hazel parallel as illustrative rather than Apple-attested.

rows.technology: Sparkle 2 (vs Mac App Store updates)
rows.claim: Sparkle 2 is the standard non-MAS macOS updater — EdDSA-signed appcast, delta updates (new format in 2.7), refreshed update UI in 2.8 — and supports notarized, hardened-runtime, and sandboxed apps, hostable as appcast.xml + notarized DMGs on existing static hosting with no backend.
rows.primary_source: NONE (Sparkle is third-party, not an Apple framework). Authoritative vendor docs: https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/ — 'Sparkle Documentation' (EdDSA/ed25519 signing, hardened-runtime/notarization, sandboxing guide) and https://sparkle-project.org/documentation/upgrading/ ('Sparkle 2.7 introduces a new format for delta updates'; 'Sparkle 2.8 introduces a refreshed UI').
rows.availability: Non-MAS macOS apps; supports sandboxed and hardened-runtime/notarized apps; no Apple entitlement (uses XPC installer helpers); runs on any modern macOS.
rows.distribution_impact: Enables in-app auto-update for the Developer ID DMG (pairs with F20); host appcast.xml + notarized DMGs on desktidy.vercel.app static hosting with zero backend.
rows.permissions: EdDSA (ed25519) signing-key management; no TCC prompt. Sandboxed builds must follow Sparkle's XPC-service sandboxing entitlement guide.
rows.fail_closed: EdDSA signature verification is mandatory, so a tampered or unreachable appcast/archive does not install — Sparkle fails closed on update.
rows.privacy: The appcast fetch is the only outbound call and can leak coarse version/usage signals unless disabled; must be disclosed and made toggleable to keep the 'your files never leave your Mac' line honest.
rows.testability: Add Sparkle to a test .app, generate an EdDSA keypair, publish a two-version appcast.xml + notarized DMGs on static hosting, and confirm the app detects, signature-verifies, and installs the delta update; then disable automatic checks and confirm (via a network monitor) that no outbound request occurs.
rows.corrections: All Sparkle claims verified against Sparkle's own current docs — but primary_source is NOT an Apple document; this is authoritative-vendor DOCUMENTED, not Apple-DOCUMENTED. The finding's own honesty note is correct and load-bearing: the update check is a network call that contradicts a literal 'zero network' marketing claim, so the invariant is threatened until the copy is reworded and the check ships opt-out.

rows.technology: Liquid Glass design language (macOS 26)
rows.claim: Recompiling against the Xcode 26 SDK gives standard AppKit/SwiftUI controls the Liquid Glass look automatically on macOS 26; custom chrome uses glassEffect/GlassEffectContainer; and the Info.plist opt-out UIDesignRequiresCompatibility is temporary, which Apple says will be removed in the next major release (Xcode 27).
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/adopting-liquid-glass — 'Adopting Liquid Glass' (Apple Developer Documentation); opt-out removal Apple-DTS-confirmed at https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/802419 (DTS Engineer Ed Ford: 'We intend this option to be removed in the next major release.').
rows.availability: macOS 26 (Tahoe) built with the Xcode 26 SDK; glassEffect / GlassEffectContainer / glassEffectID are macOS 26+ SwiftUI APIs; no hardware gate, no entitlement.
rows.distribution_impact: A brand-new menu-bar app built on Xcode 26 ships modern by default with zero legacy chrome to migrate; author the app icon in Icon Composer. No distribution restriction.
rows.permissions: None.
rows.fail_closed: Cosmetic/rendering only; no data-mutation path, so it cannot violate never-delete/never-overwrite.
rows.privacy: None — rendering only, no data touched.
rows.testability: Create a SwiftUI MenuBarExtra app, build against the Xcode 26 SDK with no UIDesignRequiresCompatibility key, and confirm the toolbar/popover render Liquid Glass material on macOS 26; add one glassEffect custom view and confirm it compiles and renders.
rows.corrections: The finding cites only a secondary blog (donnywals), but the substance is Apple-primary-confirmed: the 'Adopting Liquid Glass' doc plus DTS thread 802419 confirm the opt-out is 'removed in the next major release.' Minor wording: Apple says 'next major release' (which the finding fairly reads as Xcode 27); secondary sources phrase it as 'ignored when building against the iOS/macOS 27 SDK.' No material overstatement.

rows.technology: Spotlight redesign: actions, quick keys, clipboard history, file browsing (macOS Tahoe 26)
rows.claim: macOS Tahoe 26's Spotlight runs hundreds of actions directly — including third-party actions any app supplies via the App Intents API — assigns 'quick keys' abbreviations, adds browse views and clipboard history, and ranks results intelligently, with Shortcuts now able to auto-run on file-save-to-folder.
rows.primary_source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/macos-tahoe-26-makes-the-mac-more-capable-productive-and-intelligent-than-ever/ — Apple Newsroom (macOS Tahoe 26): 'hundreds of actions directly from Spotlight', 'quick keys', 'clipboard history', 'browse views', results 'ranked intelligently', 'any app can provide actions to Spotlight using the App Intents API', and Shortcuts running 'when ... saving a file to a folder'. (API contract for the developer surface is the App Intents doc in F24.)
rows.availability: macOS 26 Tahoe; the Spotlight actions/quick-keys/clipboard/browse-view/ranking features are user-facing system behavior; surfacing DeskTidy actions requires adopting App Intents. No special hardware.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires the .app with declared App Intents to surface DeskTidy actions in Spotlight; effectively free once the intents in F24 exist. Marketable as 'control DeskTidy from Spotlight.'
rows.permissions: None beyond the app; declared App Intents surface in Spotlight automatically.
rows.fail_closed: DeskTidy's Spotlight actions map to intents that route through the logged/undoable move engine; no destructive default.
rows.privacy: Local; DeskTidy's exposure is limited to the actions it declares. Spotlight's clipboard history is a system feature outside DeskTidy's scope.
rows.testability: Ship a macOS 26 app declaring a 'Tidy Desktop Now' AppIntent with a parameter summary, then confirm it appears in Spotlight's Actions browse view and receives an auto-assigned quick key.
rows.corrections: Apple Newsroom (a primary Apple source, though marketing rather than an API contract) confirms actions, quick keys, browse views, clipboard history, intelligent ranking, App-Intents-provided actions, and folder-save Shortcuts automations. Two specifics in the finding are NOT in the Apple source and rest on secondary reporting — the 'quick keys up to 12 chars' limit and 'clipboard history 7-day retention since 26.1' — both BELIEVED, not Apple-attested.

rows.technology: App Intents advances (Spotlight invocation on Mac, UndoableIntent, interactive snippets)
rows.claim: WWDC25 made Spotlight a first-class App Intents client on macOS and added the UndoableIntent protocol (macOS 26.0+, register undo actions via its undoManager) plus interactive snippets (live result views with buttons/toggles), letting DeskTidy's TidyNow/Pause/Resume/UndoLastMove verbs map onto system-native undo.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents/undoableintent — 'UndoableIntent' (Apple Developer Documentation; abstract 'An interface you use to register undoable actions in your app intent code'; availability iOS 26.0+ / macOS 26.0+); session context https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/275/ — 'Explore new advances in App Intents'.
rows.availability: macOS 26.0+ (also iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst/tvOS/visionOS/watchOS 26.0+) for UndoableIntent; Spotlight App Intents invocation on macOS 26. No hardware gate, no entitlement.
rows.distribution_impact: Requires the .app (App Intents needs a bundle, not the bare CLI); once present, the verbs surface for free in Spotlight, Shortcuts, and Siri. Highest-leverage Tahoe API for DeskTidy.
rows.permissions: None beyond the app; intents run in-process.
rows.fail_closed: UndoableIntent maps directly onto the existing collision-safe, everything-logged move engine — undo becomes system-native and no action deletes or overwrites.
rows.privacy: Local; intents expose only the declared verbs, with no data egress.
rows.testability: Implement a macOS 26 UndoLastMove intent conforming to UndoableIntent, register the reverse move on its undoManager, run TidyNow then invoke system undo, and confirm the last move is reversed; also return an interactive snippet from TidyNow carrying a Pause toggle.
rows.corrections: The finding cited only a WWDC video (session 260), but the actual API contract exists and verifies: UndoableIntent is a documented public protocol (macOS 26.0+), upgrading this claim from BELIEVED to DOCUMENTED. Minor: the App Intents advances session is 275 ('Explore new advances in App Intents'), not 260; UndoableIntent, interactive snippets, and Spotlight invocation are all real and Apple-documented.

rows.technology: Shortcuts automations on Mac + intelligent actions (Use Model)
rows.claim: macOS Tahoe 26 Shortcuts runs shortcuts automatically (time of day, file saved to a folder, display connected) and adds intelligent actions that tap Apple Intelligence on-device, Private Cloud Compute, or ChatGPT, so DeskTidy can ship a documented sample folder-trigger automation invoking the CLI.
rows.primary_source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/macos-tahoe-26-makes-the-mac-more-capable-productive-and-intelligent-than-ever/ — "macOS Tahoe 26 Makes the Mac More Capable, Productive, and Intelligent Than Ever" (Apple Newsroom). Action name confirmed in "Use Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts on Mac", support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchl91750563/mac.
rows.availability: macOS 26 (Tahoe), shipping (this Mac runs 26.6). Use Model on-device/PCC requires an Apple Intelligence-capable Apple Silicon Mac with AI enabled; Apple Intelligence is not available in all languages/regions. ChatGPT model is an optional extension. Folder-trigger + shell step needs only Shortcuts itself.
rows.distribution_impact: None — it is user-facing Shortcuts UX, not app code. DeskTidy ships a documented/importable sample automation; no App Store, entitlement, or notarization change. Works with the Homebrew CLI as-is.
rows.permissions: Running a shell step from Shortcuts requires the user to enable Allow Running Scripts in Shortcuts Settings > Advanced; the invoked desktidy binary keeps its existing Full Disk Access grant. Automations themselves are user-created and user-approved.
rows.fail_closed: Yes for DeskTidy's use: if the automation fails to fire, nothing runs and the Desktop is simply untouched; the triggered sweep is the same deterministic, logged, never-delete pipeline. The sample automation should contain no model step, so no probabilistic output is in the mutation path.
rows.privacy: Folder-trigger + Run Shell Script is fully local. Use Model can send prompt content to Private Cloud Compute or ChatGPT if the user selects those models — DeskTidy's sample automation must not include a model action, keeping the local-only core intact.
rows.testability: ~15 min on this macOS 26.6 Mac: build the automation 'When file added to ~/Desktop -> Run Shell Script: /opt/homebrew/bin/desktidy sweep', enable Allow Running Scripts, drop a test file, confirm the move appears in the DeskTidy log. This exact combination has not yet been live-probed.
rows.corrections: Roadmap holds. Two nuances: (1) the newsroom release never uses the name 'Use Model' — that name comes from Apple's Shortcuts support guide (support.apple.com, Apple-authored but outside the strict developer.apple.com/newsroom definition); (2) the specific folder-trigger→Run Shell Script chain is asserted, not yet demonstrated — the shell step requires an explicit Allow Running Scripts opt-in the roadmap did not mention.

rows.technology: Foundation Models framework (on-device LLM API)
rows.claim: Foundation Models is a released Swift framework (macOS 26.0+, beta:false) for the on-device Apple Intelligence model with structured output via the Generable protocol/guided generation, tool calling, and streaming, letting DeskTidy return a typed {category, confidence, reason} triage suggestion instead of free text.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels — "Foundation Models" (Apple Developer Documentation); Generable protocol at developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/generable and article "Generating Swift data structures with guided generation".
rows.availability: macOS 26.0+ (also iOS/iPadOS/visionOS 26.0, watchOS 27 beta), verified beta:false in Apple's doc metadata. Requires Apple Silicon with Apple Intelligence enabled; not available in all regions/languages; Intel Macs and AI-disabled Macs must take the fallback path. Xcode 26 to build.
rows.distribution_impact: Framework link only — no extra entitlement for basic use; works in the current SwiftPM/CLI build. The existing blocker (paid Apple ID not in Xcode) affects app distribution, not local Foundation Models use.
rows.permissions: No TCC prompt for model inference itself; availability gate via SystemLanguageModel.default.availability. DeskTidy passes only file names/metadata it already reads under FDA.
rows.fail_closed: Yes: the documented availability check lets DeskTidy degrade cleanly to the deterministic unknown→Inbox path when the model is unavailable, and guided generation eliminates the free-text parse-failure mode; suggestions never auto-move files.
rows.privacy: Inference is entirely on-device (the framework's core promise); no file contents or names leave the Mac. This is the strongest possible fit with DeskTidy's local-only core.
rows.testability: 10-line Swift spike on this macOS 26.6 Mac: check SystemLanguageModel availability, define one @Generable struct {suggestedCategory, confidence, reason}, prompt with a sample filename, assert a typed response decodes. DeskTidy's SmartTriage.swift already exercises most of this path.
rows.corrections: Core claim fully documented and current. The WWDC26 preview sub-claim is real — Apple's WWDC26 Apple Intelligence guide (developer.apple.com/wwdc26/guides/apple-intelligence/) confirms multimodal prompts and a Language Model protocol admitting third-party/cloud models — but that page states no OS version, so 'for the following OS cycle' is an inference (BELIEVED), and none of it should be built against yet.

rows.technology: Apple Intelligence user-facing features in Tahoe (Live Translation, Reminders auto-sorting, AI Spotlight)
rows.claim: Tahoe's user-facing AI (Live Translation in Messages/FaceTime/Phone, Reminders action-item suggestions, Genmoji/Image Playground, upgraded Spotlight) does not auto-organize or auto-file the user's files, leaving DeskTidy's 'macOS still won't clean your Desktop' positioning honest — there is no API to adopt.
rows.primary_source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/macos-tahoe-26-makes-the-mac-more-capable-productive-and-intelligent-than-ever/ — "macOS Tahoe 26 Makes the Mac More Capable, Productive, and Intelligent Than Ever" (Apple Newsroom).
rows.availability: macOS 26 (Tahoe), shipped Sept 2025; Apple Intelligence features require supported Apple Silicon and are region/language-limited. Irrelevant to DeskTidy's build — nothing is integrated.
rows.distribution_impact: None — positioning/marketing only; no code, no entitlement, no distribution change.
rows.permissions: None.
rows.fail_closed: Not applicable technically; the marketing claim itself fails closed if worded as 'Tahoe's announced features don't file your Desktop' rather than an absolute negative about all of macOS.
rows.privacy: No data flows added. Using the comparison in marketing copy has no privacy surface.
rows.testability: 10-minute doc pass before publishing the marketing line: re-read the current macOS 26.6 feature page/release notes and confirm no auto-filing feature has since appeared; optionally screenshot Spotlight leaving files in place on this Mac.
rows.corrections: The positive claims (Live Translation, Reminders action items, Genmoji/Image Playground, Spotlight upgrades) are all in the newsroom release. Two softenings: 'AI-ranked Spotlight results' is a paraphrase — the release emphasizes Spotlight actions and intelligence, not a ranking API; and 'nothing auto-organizes files' is inference-from-absence in one document (BELIEVED as a universal negative), so keep the marketing line scoped to announced features. Verdict is DEFER (nothing to adopt), not REJECT — no invariant is threatened.

rows.technology: Finder folder customization: tag-driven folder colors + emoji/SF Symbol folder icons
rows.claim: Tahoe Finder tints folders by their color tag (toggleable) and a new Customize Folder command adds an emoji or SF Symbol, stored in extended attribute com.apple.icon.folder#S as trivial JSON ({"emoji":"📸"} / {"sym":"doc"}) with the S (syncable) flag, so a 'desktidy decorate' step can color-tag and emoji-badge its nine destination folders via pure xattr writes.
rows.primary_source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/macos-tahoe-26-makes-the-mac-more-capable-productive-and-intelligent-than-ever/ — feature only ("Users can also change the colors of folders and add a symbol or emoji"). For the xattr mechanism: NONE — no Apple documentation exists; best secondary is https://eclecticlight.co/2025/09/18/customising-folders-in-tahoe/ (Howard Oakley, "Customising folders in Tahoe").
rows.availability: macOS 26+ for tinting and emoji/symbol icons (color tags themselves are long-standing). The #S flag (XATTR_FLAG_SYNCABLE — confirmed in the local SDK's xattr_flags.h) makes the badge iCloud-syncable. This dev Mac runs 26.6.
rows.distribution_impact: None — plain xattr writes from the existing CLI; no new entitlement, no App Store implication. But because the xattr format is undocumented, Apple can change it in any release; ship decorate as opt-in and non-essential.
rows.permissions: No permissions beyond the file access DeskTidy already has (FDA); locally verified that writing com.apple.icon.folder#S succeeds and round-trips on macOS 26.6.
rows.fail_closed: Yes: a failed or ignored xattr write leaves the folder undecorated — purely cosmetic, reversible (delete the xattr), touches no file contents, and never gates the sweep itself.
rows.privacy: Local metadata only; the only nuance is the S flag deliberately syncs the badge through iCloud Drive on synced folders — cosmetic, not content.
rows.testability: 15 min on this macOS 26.6 Mac: (1) run Finder's Customize Folder on a test folder and read back the xattr to confirm Apple writes com.apple.icon.folder#S with that JSON; (2) write the xattr programmatically on a second folder and visually confirm Finder renders the emoji. Step (1) is the load-bearing check; the write half already passed.
rows.corrections: The feature is Apple-documented (newsroom) but the entire adoption mechanism — the xattr name, JSON schema, and 'immediately shippable' framing — rests on eclecticlight.co (secondary, reverse-engineered) and is not in any Apple doc; roadmap presented it with documented-level confidence. Partially observed locally (macOS 26.6 accepts and round-trips the xattr; XATTR_FLAG_SYNCABLE is real SDK API) but Finder-side write/render is unverified, so run the 15-minute probe before shipping, and treat the format as changeable-without-notice.

rows.technology: Desktop widgets (WidgetKit on macOS)
rows.claim: WidgetKit is released Apple API (framework macOS 11.0+; desktop widgets since Sonoma) letting a Mac app bundle a widget extension whose interactivity is limited to App Intents-backed buttons/toggles, sufficient for a 'Tidied 47 files this week' widget with a Pause toggle — post-v1, inside the menu-bar app.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit — "WidgetKit" (Apple Developer Documentation); interactivity contract at "Adding interactivity to widgets and Live Activities" (developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit/adding-interactivity-to-widgets-and-live-activities).
rows.availability: WidgetKit on macOS 11.0+ (verified beta:false); desktop placement since macOS 14 Sonoma; Tahoe adds accented/tinted rendering (widgetAccentedRenderingMode). Requires a real .app bundle — gated on the menu-bar app existing, and store distribution gated on the known paid-Apple-ID blocker.
rows.distribution_impact: Widget extension must ship inside a signed app bundle (Developer ID or App Store) — cannot ship via the Homebrew CLI alone. Local development signing suffices for the spike; distribution inherits the existing paid-Apple-ID blocker.
rows.permissions: None special; the extension runs sandboxed and shares stats with the app via an App Group container. Pause toggle reuses the PauseTidying/ResumeTidying App Intents.
rows.fail_closed: Yes: the widget is a read-only stats snapshot plus an App Intent toggle; on failure it shows a stale timeline and the toggle simply doesn't change state — it can never move, delete, or overwrite files.
rows.privacy: Stats and last-moves data stay in the local App Group container; nothing leaves the Mac.
rows.testability: Half-day spike once the app target exists: add a widget extension with a hardcoded stats view, run dev-signed on this macOS 26.6 Mac, place it on the Desktop, then wire one AppIntent toggle. No probe needed to trust the API itself.
rows.corrections: Roadmap cited only WWDC25 session 278 ("What's new in widgets") — an Apple video, not an API contract; the primary WidgetKit documentation now located confirms every claim, so status upgrades from video-sourced to DOCUMENTED. Minor precision: the WidgetKit framework is macOS 11+, with 14 (Sonoma) being when widgets reached the Desktop; sequencing after App Intents remains correct since the toggle reuses them.

rows.technology: Controls (ControlWidget) in macOS Tahoe Control Center / menu bar
rows.claim: ControlWidget (a SwiftUI protocol, iOS 18.0+ and macOS 26.0+, released not beta) lets an app ship App Intents-backed toggle/button controls placeable in system spaces including Control Center — ideal for a DeskTidy Active/Paused toggle — but early-Tahoe third-party controls were missing from the Control Center gallery, so placement must be probed on the current build before committing.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/controlwidget — "ControlWidget" (Apple Developer Documentation); implementation article "Creating controls to perform actions across the system" (developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit/creating-controls-to-perform-actions-across-the-system).
rows.availability: macOS 26.0+ (verified beta:false; also iOS/iPadOS 18.0+, watchOS 26.0+). Requires the menu-bar app with a widget extension and the App Intents in place; menu-bar/Control Center placement is a Tahoe system-customization feature.
rows.distribution_impact: Same as F29: ships only inside a signed app bundle, not the Homebrew CLI; mostly-declarative code on top of existing intents, so marginal cost is small once the app and App Intents exist.
rows.permissions: None special; the control invokes the PauseTidying/ResumeTidying App Intents through the system, no extra TCC.
rows.fail_closed: Yes: a SetValueIntent-backed toggle that fails leaves state unchanged and the control merely displays stale state; pause/resume only gates whether DeskTidy acts — failure can never cause a file mutation.
rows.privacy: State is a single local boolean; nothing leaves the Mac.
rows.testability: Half-day spike on this macOS 26.6 Mac: dev-signed app with one ControlWidget toggle; verify it appears in the Control Center/menu-bar gallery WITHOUT the Edit-Widgets refresh workaround, and that toggling round-trips through the intent. This probe is exactly why SPIKE rather than ADOPT.
rows.corrections: API claim upgrades from WWDC-video-sourced to DOCUMENTED — note ControlWidget lives in SwiftUI, not WidgetKit as the roadmap implied. The gallery-bug claim rests on MacStories (secondary): their follow-up "Mystery Solved" piece (macstories.net) reframed it as a stale-gallery-cache bug with a user workaround (right-click Desktop > Edit Widgets forces a refresh) — it was MacStories calling it a bug, never Apple-acknowledged as the roadmap's wording suggested, and whether 26.6 still exhibits it is UNKNOWN until the spike runs.

rows.technology: Live Activities on Mac (ActivityKit)
rows.claim: On macOS 26 Tahoe, Live Activities from a user's nearby iPhone appear in the Mac menu bar and open in iPhone Mirroring when clicked; Apple documents no macOS-native ActivityKit lane for a Mac app to originate its own Live Activity (ActivityKit platform availability lists only iOS 16.1+, iPadOS 16.1+, Mac Catalyst 16.1+).
rows.primary_source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/macos-tahoe-26-makes-the-mac-more-capable-productive-and-intelligent-than-ever/ — "macOS Tahoe 26 makes the Mac more capable, productive, and intelligent than ever" (Apple Newsroom, June 9 2025); plus https://developer.apple.com/documentation/activitykit — "ActivityKit" (platform matrix, no macOS entry; abstract: Live Activities "on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and the Mac"; article "Displaying live data with Live Activities" says display surface is "a paired Mac")
rows.availability: Mac display surface: macOS 26 Tahoe with a nearby paired iPhone (click-through requires iPhone Mirroring). ActivityKit API: iOS 16.1+ / iPadOS 16.1+ / Mac Catalyst 16.1+; no macOS-native availability. No entitlement relevant to DeskTidy.
rows.distribution_impact: None — not adopted. DeskTidy has no iOS app to originate an activity from, so nothing ships.
rows.permissions: None for DeskTidy. User-side feature requires iPhone pairing/Continuity, outside app control.
rows.fail_closed: Nothing adopted, no failure path introduced; 'tidying in progress' status stays on the existing widget + menu-bar item, which work without any paired device.
rows.privacy: No DeskTidy data involved; mirrored Live Activity content flows through Apple's Continuity channel between the user's own devices.
rows.testability: On a Tahoe Mac paired with an iPhone, start any Live Activity on the iPhone and observe it in the Mac menu bar; separately add `import ActivityKit` to a native (non-Catalyst) macOS target and confirm it does not build, proving no Mac-origination lane.
rows.corrections: Original citation was WWDC25 video session 278 ("What's new in widgets") — Apple-authored but not an API contract; replaced with Apple Newsroom + ActivityKit reference docs. One nuance the roadmap flattened: ActivityKit does list Mac Catalyst 16.1 availability (symbols compile in Catalyst apps), so the precise statement is 'no documented macOS-native origination lane; Apple describes the Mac only as a mirrored display surface for a paired iPhone', not literally 'no API surface exists on Mac'. Verdict skip→DEFER (no invariant violation; re-evaluate only if Apple ships Mac-native Live Activities).

rows.technology: FSKit (user-space file systems)
rows.claim: FSKit (macOS 15.4+, non-beta) is Apple's framework to "implement a file system that runs in user space" via app extensions — a facility for providing volumes, which DeskTidy (a deterministic mover on the user's existing APFS home volume) never needs.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/fskit — "FSKit" (platforms: macOS 15.4, beta:false; abstract: "Implement a file system that runs in user space.")
rows.availability: macOS 15.4+; delivered as an app extension hosted in an app; no special hardware, region, or Apple-granted entitlement.
rows.distribution_impact: None (deferred). If ever adopted it would force an app-extension host app, incompatible with the brew-CLI distribution story.
rows.permissions: User enables the file-system extension in System Settings; nothing applies to DeskTidy as-is.
rows.fail_closed: Not adopted; no failure path. DeskTidy mounts nothing.
rows.privacy: N/A — no data implications for DeskTidy; noted only so the option isn't revisited.
rows.testability: Build and run Apple's FSKitSample on the current 26.x and attempt a mount; success or an extensionKit errorDomain Code=2 failure settles in minutes whether the reported third-party FSKit breakage persists.
rows.corrections: The core framework claim (user-space FS, since macOS 15.4) is DOCUMENTED from the cited primary doc, which was correct. The 'third-party FSKit extensions broken on macOS 26 by an Apple bug' sub-claim rests only on community GitHub issues (macfuse/macfuse#1132, andrewgazelka/loaf#1, reported against 26.1/26.2; extensionKit errorDomain Code=2, reproduces even with Apple's FSKitSample) — no Apple acknowledgment found, so that part is BELIEVED and possibly stale on today's 26.6. Irrelevant to the verdict either way: DeskTidy needs no volumes. Verdict skip→DEFER (out of scope, not invariant-violating).

rows.technology: File Provider + NSFileProviderSearching (Tahoe cloud-file Spotlight search)
rows.claim: macOS 26 adds NSFileProviderSearching (macOS 26.0+), "a protocol you implement to support searching in your file provider," letting Spotlight surface third-party-provider documents including non-downloaded ones — an API for cloud-storage vendors, which local-only DeskTidy is not.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/fileprovider/nsfileprovidersearching — "NSFileProviderSearching" (platforms: macOS 26.0, beta:false, deprecated:false)
rows.availability: macOS 26.0+; implemented inside an NSFileProviderReplicatedExtension (macOS 11+); adoption is per-vendor (Dropbox/Drive/OneDrive must implement it); no restricted entitlement.
rows.distribution_impact: None (deferred) — DeskTidy ships no File Provider extension.
rows.permissions: Provider extensions are user-enabled; DeskTidy needs nothing new.
rows.fail_closed: Operational implication adopted into the status quo: the watcher must keep treating dataless/materializing provider files conservatively (existing 15s settle window; never move a file that isn't fully local) so a provider-backed Desktop/Documents can never cause a premature move — fail-closed preserved.
rows.privacy: No DeskTidy data leaves the machine; building a provider lane would sit against the local-only core, which is exactly why it's skipped.
rows.testability: On Tahoe with a provider app installed, Spotlight-search a non-downloaded provider document to see the feature; for DeskTidy's side, place a dataless file in a watched folder and confirm the watcher defers action until it materializes.
rows.corrections: Original citation was Computerworld (secondary; verified it does make the provider-search claim). The roadmap's hedge 'reported as NSFileProviderSearching' can be dropped: the protocol exists under exactly that name with macOS 26.0 availability on developer.apple.com. The consumer-facing 'per-provider Spotlight location filters' detail remains secondary-sourced (BELIEVED). Verdict skip→DEFER; the conservative-watcher implication is already satisfied by the current engine.

rows.technology: File-system event APIs beyond FSEvents / launchd WatchPaths (Endpoint Security)
rows.claim: FSEvents + launchd WatchPaths remain the sanctioned general-purpose file-event primitives on Tahoe (no new alternative found in Apple's Tahoe docs), and the only richer option — Endpoint Security (macOS 10.15+) — requires a system extension plus the com.apple.developer.endpoint-security.client entitlement, which Apple's doc says "you must request … from Apple."
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.endpoint-security.client — "com.apple.developer.endpoint-security.client" (macOS 10.15+; "You must request this entitlement from Apple"); plus https://developer.apple.com/documentation/endpointsecurity — "Endpoint Security" (macOS 10.15+). For the negative claim (no new file-event API) there is no primary Apple statement — it is an inference from absence.
rows.availability: FSEvents/WatchPaths: all supported macOS, unrestricted. Endpoint Security: macOS 10.15+, Apple-granted restricted entitlement, system-extension packaging, Developer ID distribution — aimed at security vendors.
rows.distribution_impact: Status quo: zero impact, brew-from-source story intact. ES adoption would require a notarized app bundle + admin-approved system extension install, killing the lightweight distribution — a further reason not to pursue it.
rows.permissions: Status quo: user LaunchAgent only. ES would add: Apple entitlement grant, admin system-extension approval, and typically Full Disk Access.
rows.fail_closed: The validated FSEvents + WatchPaths + 15s-settle architecture keeps the fail-closed watcher semantics unchanged on Tahoe; no migration, no new failure modes.
rows.privacy: FSEvents path observes only the watched folders; ES would ingest process-attributed events system-wide — far more data than DeskTidy needs, cutting against data-minimal local-only design.
rows.testability: Already reproduced on this machine: macOS 26.6 (build 25G70) with the com.sicarii.desktop-autosort LaunchAgent loaded at exit status 0 and actively filing Desktop drops — the spike is `launchctl list | grep autosort` plus dropping a file on ~/Desktop and watching it get sorted.
rows.corrections: Original citation was an Objective-See blog (secondary); the Endpoint Security half is re-grounded in Apple's primary entitlement + framework docs (DOCUMENTED), and 'the current architecture still works on Tahoe' is OBSERVED live on this macOS 26.6 Mac. The row is marked BELIEVED because its load-bearing sentence — 'Tahoe adds no new general-purpose file-event API' — is a negative claim no Apple page states; it is a reasoned inference from absence in current documentation. Verdict skip→DEFER (validated status quo; ES doesn't violate invariants, it's simply disproportionate and practically unobtainable).

rows.technology: Intel sunset: Tahoe last Intel macOS; Rosetta wind-down
rows.claim: Apple's macOS Tahoe 26.4 Release Notes state: "macOS Tahoe 26 is the last release to support Intel based Macs. Additionally, Rosetta support for apps will end after macOS 27. Starting in macOS Tahoe 26.4, users will be notified when they launch apps that use Rosetta of the upcoming incompatibility," with continued support only for older unmaintained games and Intel binaries in Linux VMs.
rows.primary_source: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/macos-release-notes/macos-26_4-release-notes — "macOS Tahoe 26.4 Release Notes"; corroborated by https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apple-silicon/about-the-rosetta-translation-environment — "About the Rosetta translation environment" ("available through macOS 27"; macOS 27 integrates Intel Linux-binary translation without installing Rosetta) and https://support.apple.com/en-us/124963 (allowRosettaUsageAwareness MDM key)
rows.availability: Platform lifecycle policy, no API/entitlement: Intel Macs top out at Tahoe 26.x; Rosetta app support through macOS 27; 26.4+ shows launch warnings for Rosetta apps (MDM-suppressible via allowRosettaUsageAwareness).
rows.distribution_impact: Adopt the decision now: brew CLI builds from source so it is naturally native on both architectures — keep it that way; ship the menu-bar app as a universal (arm64+x86_64) binary targeting macOS 26+; never ship anything x86_64-only (26.4 launch warnings would stigmatize it); plan the arm64-only cut around the macOS 28 timeframe.
rows.permissions: None.
rows.fail_closed: Universal binary means DeskTidy never depends on Rosetta, so the wind-down cannot degrade it; even post-cut, Intel holdouts on Tahoe keep a working brew build-from-source path (compiles natively) — no silent breakage.
rows.privacy: N/A — build/distribution policy, no data implications.
rows.testability: `lipo -archs <built binary>` to confirm universal output after setting ARCHS="arm64 x86_64"; optionally launch an x86_64-only test binary on a 26.4+ Mac and observe the Rosetta deprecation warning dialog.
rows.corrections: Original citation was MacRumors (secondary); all three sub-claims are now grounded verbatim in Apple's own 26.4 release notes — the roadmap understated its evidence rather than overstating it. Two peripheral details remain unverified against a primary page: the exact 2019–2020 Intel model enumeration and the '~2028 security updates for Intel Tahoe users' timeline (the latter is an inference from Apple's customary ~2-year security-update cadence, BELIEVED). Note precise wording: Apple says Rosetta app support ends "after macOS 27", i.e. the general capability disappears in the macOS 28 era, with a games/Linux-VM subset persisting.
